page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.metal is a bare-metal server powered by 64 physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor, running at 2.6 GHz with a dedicated CPU allocation. It features 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. It does not include any GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 20998.0 and a software compilation score of 59925.0, both placing in the top 10%. Memory performance is also strong, with a Passmark memory score in the top 10% and uncached read bandwidth reaching 277.0 GB/sec. Multi-core stress-ng CPU performance and Passmark database operations fall within the top 25%. However, single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1544.0.

The server exhibits a notable performance tradeoff in LLM workloads. While text generation for a medium 7B model is strong at 27.43 tokens/sec, text generation for a small 135M model is poor, falling into the bottom 10% at 33.83 tokens/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture provides high resource density with dedicated physical cores and integrated high-capacity NVMe storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive tasks.

This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and redis-based caching. The combination of dedicated ARM cores and local NVMe storage supports concurrent processing tasks but is less optimal for single-threaded applications or small-model LLM text generation.
